chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, said:
Intoxication is four types: intoxication from drink, intoxication from wealth, intoxication from sleep, and intoxication from rulership.
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of intoxication mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith through a chain linking Imam al-Sadiq to Imam Ali, expanding the concept of *sukr* (intoxication) beyond physical wine consumption to include spiritual and psychological states. This classification highlights how wealth, sleep, and political power can similarly cloud the intellect and heart, serving as subtle forms of distraction from divine awareness. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on inner purification, where any dominant passion that overrides reason is considered a form of intoxication.
